title: Apple Butter Takes Center Stage at This Lansing Festival - NewsBreak
text:
By JR ,
57 minutes ago
Besides maybe a potato, it’s hard to think of another food that’s quite as versatile as the apple.
You can do so much with apples: apple cider, apple pies, caramel apples, applesauce—the list goes on and on.
READ MORE: 7 Michigan Festivals Not to Miss This October
However, at the Fenner Nature Center in Lansing October 18-19, it’s all about apple butter.
Ever tried apple butter bars? Yeah – these look kind of amazing. (Photo via Unsplash – Sheri Silver) 2025 marks the 51st annual Apple Butter Festival at Fenner Nature Center, with a wide variety of activities planned for the whole family.
What Exactly Is Apple Butter? If you’ve never tried apple butter, you might not know that technically it’s not really “butter”. There’s no dairy involved at all. It’s more of a thick, rich spread made by mixing cooked apples with cider, sugar and spices, and stirred until it’s at a consistency similar to that of butter.
Taste, Learn, and Take Home Fresh Apple Butter In addition to sampling apple butter and learning exactly how it’s made, those who attend the festival will have the opportunity to take some fresh apple butter home as well.
Download the WITL Mobile App Now The Apple Butter Festival will also feature artisan demonstrations, local vendors, food trucks, musicians, and a variety of hands-on activities. Cider and donuts will be available for purchase as well.
Festival Times and Location Fenner Nature Center is located in Lansing near the intersection of E. Mount Hope Avenue and Aurelius Road. The Apple Butter Festival will be held both Saturday and Sunday from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. each day.
5 Quirky But Fun Festivals Around Michigan Gallery Credit: Tommy McNeill Getty Images Mesick Mushroom Festival - Mesick, MI The small village of Mesick in Springfield Township is known as the Mushroom Capital of the World, recognized as the premier location for finding morel mushrooms. This edible mushroom is difficult to find but grows in abundance in the Mesick area. Each Mother's Day Weekend, they host the Mesick Mushroom Festival, drawing in mushroom hunters from around the country to find these elusive shrooms. Omer Suckerfest via Facebook Suckerfest - Omer, MI When I initially heard of Suckerfest, I got excited, thinking there was an entire festival dedicated to lollipops. But no, this is a far more Michigan experience. Omer, Michigan's smallest city, hosts a fishing tournament on the Rifle River with a $1,200 cash prize for the biggest fish caught. In 2024, the prize went to a 14-year-old, so this competition is truly open to everyone. If fishing isn't your thing, there's also a parade and market. Getty Images Mac and Cheese Festival - Kalamazoo & Traverse City Mac and Cheese is a meal many of us have been eating since we were kids, but there's a more profound sense of enjoyment in eating mac and cheese when you realize it can be made far better than just a box. Kalamazoo knows this, which is why it hosts the Mac and Cheese Festival each year. Promising lots of mac and cheese, beer, and music. Last year, it was held in Traverse City for the first time, too. Upper Peninsula Supply Co. via Facebook Plaidurday - Marquette, MI The most Yooper festival imaginable, where the only rule for entry is that you must wear plaid. It's that simple. Yoopers gather to hang out, wearing plaid, and then all cluster together to take a photo of the plaid. 2025 drew in 964 people. Grab a beer, wear your best plaid, and hang out by Lake Superior. Cheeseburger in Caseville Festival via Facebook Cheeseburger Festival - Caseville, MI Originally a three-day event, the Caseville Cheeseburger Festival is now a 10-day-long festival that features a wide range of burger stands, but also live tropical music, vendors, a petting zoo, and a massive parade. It's just like Jimmy Buffett's classic song, "Cheeseburgers in Caseville" or something like that.
